review_items.rationale:
Reviewed fixed artifact bb4b2c5713754168a8dfc3d95058259d version 1 and its accepted C_accepted_phase_report requirement, retained source bindings, harness, plan, raw CheckRun 5889f79a2ba84d4dbf016630607560c4 events and monitor assessment. The check asks whether actual successfully accepted support is reported as ACCEPTED-or-later by a subsequent promise-only Prepare. handleAcceptReply consumes matching positive replies as commit support; handlePrepare exposes the local phase; handlePrepareReply uses ACCEPTED to resume acceptance without the preaccept classification rules. The PreAccept guards and recovery conflict code distinguish accepted support from preaccepted support. This establishes the local representation duty independently of a global agreement theorem. Mere enum naming is not the grounding.

The history is produced by actual handlers and serializers. With N=5,F=2 and thriftiness on, origin 2 first creates PUT(key=9,value=20), while its outgoing PreAccepts to 3/4 remain pending. Origin 1 creates PUT(key=9,value=42) and sends PreAccept to 0/2. Peer 0 has no prior conflict; peer 2 has its own pending conflicting instance. Their actual replies drive origin 1 into ACCEPTED rather than commitment, which the harness checks before reading the actual Accept frames. Both peer handlers are checked to have a non-stale request and a status below COMMITTED, then execute handleAccept. Each decoded AcceptReply is verified against the request identity and ballot; each local bal/vbal/seq/deps is checked against the accepted request. Only then are the replies processed at the origin. Origin status must actually reach COMMITTED after those replies. No accepted phase is seeded, and the positive-support event cannot be emitted on an unreached prefix.

The fresh bounded replicas initialize used fields like New: empty slot arrays, -1 prefixes, empty conflict maps, actual RPC registration order, F=2, thrifty=true and Dreply=true. All handlers and buffers run on one test goroutine; no concurrent fields or shutdown snapshots are observed. Reduced slot capacity is enough for slot 0 in two origin rows. In-memory peer writers still invoke actual SendMsg, frame byte, Marshal, New and Unmarshal. The chosen peer permutations are compatible with UpdatePreferredPeerOrder/ComputeClosestPeers. The proposal identities are data, not the operation-correlation oracle. The server PROPOSE path and zero-delay DelayProposeChan admit commands without a monotonic-ID check; Client.SendProposal also accepts an explicit Propose. A nonzero artificial latency scheduler imposes additional sequencing, but it is not selected by this bounded no-delay input. No client retry or response-order responsibility is inferred.

After origin commitment, Commit frames to peers 0/2 remain buffered. This is permitted in-flight work; the check neither discards them nor requires them to have drained. Replica 2 has not installed Commit for target 1.0 and invokes the actual recovery entry for this locally uncommitted slot. It generates ballot 7 through makeBallot and broadcasts actual Prepare. Peer 0 receives that request on a separate sender link and handles only that higher promise after its eligible acceptance; no intervening operation changes its value or installs Commit. Per-link exercised message order is preserved, with unrelated traffic pending. Calling recovery directly omits watcher timing, not a value precondition of the handler. This scope does not claim a numeric recovery deadline, automatic trigger or full running deployment.

The oracle is the actual decoded report.Status >= ACCEPTED. The source enum orders NONE=0, PREACCEPTED=1, PREACCEPTED_EQ=2, ACCEPTED=3, COMMITTED=4, EXECUTED=5. Thus the boolean accepts stronger committed/executed states and does not strengthen the obligation to exact ACCEPTED. Independent input scenario selects applicability. Admission alias accepted requires actual successful acceptance and attained origin commitment. The single prerequisite and result share scenario, acceptor, origin and instance; result identity comes from the decoded report and prerequisite identity from the actual AcceptReply. Neither the phase nor sequence being inspected is used for correlation. No missing completion is treated as a failing value.

Raw execution reports accept_ballot=1, accepted_seq=local_seq=1, local_phase=2, origin_committed=true and 57 pending Commit bytes for peer 0 / origin 1 / slot 0. The subsequent fully decoded report has request_ballot=7, reported_phase=local_phase=2, report_seq=1, accepted_or_later=false and zero remaining bytes. The monitor reports no parse errors and one complete correlated violating comparison. Process tests_passed records successful completion of the experiment, not satisfaction of the property. Source explains the result: eligible handleAccept assigns ballots and ordering attributes but omits Status, while handlePrepare faithfully copies the retained old status. The status codec is present; the separate VBallot omission does not cause this phase result.

Alternative protections remain explicit. The accepting peer has retained sequence/dependency metadata, so the result is not total loss of accepted data. A delivered Commit would advance its phase, and recovery can sometimes resume acceptance even from preaccepted support. Neither explains why this positive accepted support is reported as preaccepted in the tested allowed interval; neither is claimed to fail globally here. No issue found in correspondence for the local phase violation. This result does not demonstrate different decisions, a recovery stall, durable-history loss or an unsafe quorum formula.
